workload.model: dynamically selected loaded oMLX coding model
workload.phase: Codex Responses API inference with local tools
workload.runtime: loopback oMLX server plus Local Codex fork
workload.shape: single-user coding turns with shell, patch, MCP, image, agent, and compaction events

goal.quality_floor: loopback-only transport, no OpenAI authentication, correct context limits, and native tool behavior

evidence: Stock Codex can reach the custom oMLX provider for plain text and shell calls, but apply_patch was emitted in a tool shape the live server discarded.
The unmodified runtime also attempted curated plugin network calls, so it did not meet the local-only boundary.
diagnostics/local-codex/upstream-test-baseline.json records the one inherited upstream test failure separately from fork behavior.
Live oMLX accepted flat function tools but silently omitted raw custom tools, including the upstream freeform patch tool.
Process socket inspection found automatic remote plugin discovery before those features were disabled.
The model context window and active-model identity had to come from the live oMLX administration API rather than a fixed model table.
shared_assumptions: The oMLX server remains reachable through a loopback HTTP address.
A loaded coding-capable model advertises a nonzero context length through the oMLX administration API.

exploit: Use oMLX's native Responses endpoint and Codex's local compaction path.
Discover the loaded coding model and context limit before every launch.
subordinate: Disable update checks, doctor update probes, telemetry exporters, feedback, apps, curated plugins, remote plugins, and tool suggestions.
Keep the fork in an isolated home and preserve the stock Codex installation.
elevate: Add a function-shaped apply_patch contract and dispatcher support while preserving upstream freeform behavior for other providers.
Generate a local-only provider, model catalog, and separate editable persona at launch.

evidence: diagnostics/local-codex/live-acceptance.json records passing shell, patch, long-running shell, multi-agent, MCP, image, compaction, clear, and loopback-egress canaries.
Python generator tests and focused Rust patch-tool tests passed.
Process-level network observations during a live model turn and the installed doctor command showed no external connection.

accepted_tradeoffs: OpenAI-hosted apps, curated plugins, web services, login, cloud tasks, and updates are intentionally unavailable.
The product name remains the neutral Local Codex placeholder until the user chooses a persona name.
decision.rationale: Promote because the local-only fork passed the required native harness behaviors with the live oMLX model while preserving the stock Codex installation.

next_constraint: Compatibility verification when switching to a materially different loaded model or oMLX protocol version.

requirements.requirement: Use only the live loopback oMLX server with no OpenAI authentication or remote background services.
requirements.command: Run a live Local Codex turn while observing process sockets and inspect the isolated auth/config files.
evidence: Only 127.0.0.1 oMLX traffic was observed during model work; doctor made no external connection; auth.json is absent; remote features and telemetry exporters are disabled.

requirements.requirement: Select loaded coding models dynamically and preserve their real context limits.
requirements.command: Run prepare_runtime.py against the active oMLX administration API and inspect generated model/config files.
evidence: The active Qwen model and 262144-token context were discovered live, and the implementation contains no model slug.

requirements.requirement: Operate native coding tools, compaction, and clearing through the model-facing harness.
requirements.command: Run the recorded live shell, patch, long-shell, child-agent, MCP, image, compact, and clear canaries.
evidence: All nine acceptance surfaces passed against the loaded local model.

requirements.requirement: Keep the persona independent from IRIS and easy to rename.
requirements.command: Generate runtime instructions from persona.toml, run the persona unit test, and inspect compacted context.
evidence: The runtime persona explicitly excludes IRIS identity and changing the name requires editing one TOML field.
